Freylekhs / polka

Bass on every beat, the whole chord on every off-beat

Open the Freylekhs / polka style in the Backing Track

What it is

The fast 2/4 of Eastern European dance music: the bass on every beat, alternating root and fifth, and the full chord on every off-beat (oom-pa oom-pa). A freylekhs (“joyful”) is the most common klezmer dance tune; the polka is its Central European cousin.

A little history

The polka started in Bohemia in the 1830s and was danced across Europe and America within a decade. Its bands (brass, then accordion) gave it the bass-and-off-beat accompaniment. Klezmer is the instrumental music of Ashkenazi Jewish weddings in Eastern Europe. Immigrant clarinettists Naftule Brandwein and Dave Tarras recorded it in New York in the 1920s, with bands that played the same driving off-beats on piano, brass and drums. It faded after the war and came back in the 1970s revival (the Klezmorim, Andy Statman, Kapelye, later the Klezmatics). Songs like Hava Nagila and Hanukkah songs are still played this way.

The band’s version

  • Bass: Root and fifth on every beat, with a run up into the next bar now and then.
  • Comping: chords on the off-beats. In half-time bars the piano switches to ballad patterns.

Listening

Recording Year Listen for
Naftule Brandwein, Der Heyser Bulgar 1923 Clarinet over off-beat backing.
Dave Tarras, Dave Tarras’ Freylekhs (many dance sides) 1920s-50s New York klezmer dance band.
Frankie Yankovic, Just Because 1947 American polka.
The Klezmatics, Rhythm + Jews 1991 Revival klezmer.

More recent

Recording Year Listen for
Gogol Bordello, Start Wearing Purple 2005 Eastern European off-beats as punk.
“Weird Al” Yankovic, Polka Face (Alpocalypse) 2011 A polka medley of pop hits: bass on the beat, chords off it.

Sources

  • Henry Sapoznik, Klezmer! Jewish Music from Old World to Our World (Schirmer, 1999; 2nd ed. 2006).
  • Walter Zev Feldman, Klezmer: Music, History, and Memory (Oxford, 2016).
  • DAHR, Naftule Brandwein: Heiser bulgar, Victor, 10 May 1923.
  • Victor Greene, A Passion for Polka (California, 1992).
